summary: Maldives Immigration grants tourists a visa on arrival without pre-approval, provided they have confirmed return tickets, a prepaid confirmed booking and sufficient funds; since 15 April 2025 entry is not granted on Israeli passports. The UK and Canada say the visa is for 30 days, and Australia says it is free. Every traveller must also submit the free Imuga Traveller Declaration within 96 hours before arrival, and the stay can be extended in-country through the Imuga portal.

evidence.text: Tourist visa is granted on arrival to the Maldives. Foreigners traveling to Maldives as tourists do not require pre-approval for the visa.

fee.notes: The Maldives' Permanent Mission to the UN says a free tourist visa of up to thirty days is issued on arrival. Maldives Immigration lists the entry requirements: a machine-readable passport with at least 1 month's validity, confirmed return journey tickets, a prepaid confirmed booking at a registered facility and sufficient funds for the stay, or a sponsorship it has approved. It says entry is not granted on Israeli passports.

passportValidity.text: Your passport (or travel document) must be machine-readable and valid for at least 1 month on arrival, according to Maldives Immigration; the UK Foreign Office gives the same 1-month rule. Canada's travel advice asks for 6 months from your date of entry.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required only if you arrive from, or transited through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for the Maldives; the basic entry requirements Maldives Immigration lists for tourists do not include insurance.

onwardTicket.text: Confirmed return journey tickets are one of the entry requirements Maldives Immigration lists for tourists.

proofOfFunds.text: Maldives Immigration lists sufficient funds to cover the stay among the basic entry requirements, together with confirmed return journey tickets and a prepaid confirmed booking at a registered facility (or a sponsorship approved by Maldives Immigration); it does not publish an amount. The Maldives' Permanent Mission to the UN gives the funds as US$100 plus US$50 per day, or a confirmation of reservation in a tourist resort or hotel.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to bring in anything deemed contrary to Islam, including idols for worship, bibles, pork and pork products, and alcohol.
Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to export tortoise shell and coral.
Australia's Smartraveller says it is illegal to import pornography, alcohol or pork products, though alcohol and pork may be consumed on resort islands.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says crime is low on the resort islands, but petty theft happens — do not leave things unattended on the beach or in unlocked rooms. It says that outside the resorts there is gang-related violence, including knife crime, mainly in Malé and Hulhumalé, and advises avoiding empty roads on foot after dark. It warns that strong tidal currents can drag swimmers away from the shore and cause drownings, so ask resort staff where it is safe to swim.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says alcoholic drinks are available only on resort islands and you should not take any out of your resort: you can be arrested and deported for possessing or drinking alcohol, or being intoxicated, outside resorts and on inhabited islands. Importing alcohol is illegal.

Canada's travel advice says to dress conservatively, especially outside major cities and coastal resorts, and notes that publicly observing any religion other than Islam is illegal. The UK Foreign Office says that during Ramadan you should not eat, drink or smoke in public in the daytime outside holiday resorts.

The Imuga Traveller Declaration is free at imuga.immigration.gov.mv and must be submitted within 96 hours before your flight for arrival; the Imuga home page lists departure too. Maldives Immigration advises against other websites that may charge a fee.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for the Maldives?
faq.answer: No advance visa: Maldives Immigration grants tourists a visa on arrival without pre-approval, provided you have confirmed return tickets, a prepaid confirmed booking, sufficient funds and a submitted Imuga declaration. Entry is not granted on Israeli passports. The UK and Canada say the visa is for 30 days; Australia says it is free.

faq.question: What is the Imuga Traveller Declaration?
faq.answer: Imuga is the Maldives' online traveller declaration. Maldives Immigration says all travellers must submit it within 96 hours before their flight time for arrival, and its home page lists it as mandatory within 96 hours of arrival or departure. Submitting it at imuga.immigration.gov.mv is free.

faq.question: Can I stay in the Maldives longer than 30 days?
faq.answer: Yes. Maldives Immigration says tourists can apply for visa extensions through the IMUGA portal. Passport and accommodation details are filled in automatically (applicants who have changed accommodation can update their hotel) and a passport-size photo taken within the last 12 months is uploaded; Immigration says extension applications are now expected to be completed within 48 hours. It does not publish the maximum length of an extension or the fee.

faq.question: Can I bring alcohol into the Maldives?
faq.answer: No. Canada's travel advice says importing alcohol is illegal, and the UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to bring in alcohol. Alcohol is available only on resort islands; you can be arrested and deported for possessing or drinking it outside resorts.

faq.question: Do I need to change money into rufiyaa?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says the currency is the rufiyaa (MVR), that major credit cards are accepted at resorts and hotels, and that US dollars can be exchanged at the airport, banks and hotels. ATMs are only in Malé and the more populated non-resort islands.
